what_it_does: When a GPU (a chip with thousands of small processors originally designed for graphics) runs AI inference — that is, using a trained neural network to answer questions or classify images — much of the hardware sits idle because work arrives unevenly and the operating system hands out resources in coarse chunks. DARIS is a scheduler, meaning software that decides which task runs where and when, that carves a single GPU into spatial slices (different groups of processors handling different tasks simultaneously, via NVIDIA's Multi-Process Service) and also interleaves tasks over time using prioritized queues. A staging mechanism lets a task migrate from one slice to another with essentially zero delay. The abstract is brief, so the full performance results and exact design details are uncertain.
